name: Dark eyeliner to make iris pop

lead: Dark eyeliner along the lash line frames the eye so the iris colour looks stronger. Users want eyes that stand out, with a lighter or more saturated iris.
A dark border raises local contrast against the iris, which makes its colour read as brighter. The claim comes from makeup practice, and no research on this specific effect was found.

paras: People draw a thin line close to the upper lash line, sometimes the lower rim too, with pencil, gel or liquid liner, often with mascara. Brown, black, and colours chosen to complement the iris are common.
General eyeliner cautions apply, such as irritation or infection from contaminated products. Replacing products regularly and keeping them clean is the usual advice; specific data was not found.

angle.text: A dark line at the lash line frames the iris, and the added contrast makes its colour look more vivid straight away. This comes from makeup practice and has not been studied.

lead: Dark eyeliner to make the iris pop is a makeup practice in which dark liner is applied along the lash line to increase contrast with the iris. Practitioners say it makes eye color look more vivid.

paras: The idea is that a dark frame around the eye heightens the apparent brightness of the iris. This is a practitioner claim; no published study of the effect was identified. Eyeliner itself has a long history, dating to ancient Egypt and Mesopotamia according to Wikipedia.[1]
